correctness.rationale: The bijection between order-seven orientable cyclic words and de Bruijn closed trails with one edge per nonpalindromic reversal pair is proved in both directions, including primitivity. The 56-pair bound makes exhaustive search finite. The unrestricted root-vertex recursion records every valid closure and continues through repeated root visits; rotation quotient identifies necklaces. Exact Python and independently rooted C++17 enumerators agree on all 29 positive period counts, 4788 total necklaces, 336 maximum-length necklaces and the same 336-word certificate. Each certificate word is checked against all cyclic seven-windows, and every maximum has the claimed weight, cyclic run count and short-factor profile; finite exhaustive enumeration proves this finite claim, not an infinite extrapolation.

value.rationale: The full length-by-length cyclic census is a natural complete finite classification for the first nontrivial order at which exact maximum period36 was recently established. It distinguishes existence at one maximum length from counts across every period, reveals true impossible lengths31 and35 below that maximum, and identifies the uniform balanced, 20-run and ternary-window rigidity of all maximizers plus 90 symmetry types. These exact finite benchmarks and structural restrictions are useful for orientable position-label constructions; the result is not a routine recomputation of a published maximum length.
